goal: Determinar si existen antecedentes de restauracion de FTO por sobreexpresion o por edicion epigenetica, y que fenotipos de senescencia o de daño al ADN revierten.

questions.question: According to these sources, how does FTO overexpression protect human granulosa cells, and what specific phenotypes (senescence markers, viability, function) improve as a result?
According to these sources (e.g., FTO stabilizing MIS12), what molecular mechanism links FTO restoration to counteracting cellular senescence?

What antecedents in these sources describe reversing ovarian aging phenotypes through cell-based or molecular interventions (e.g., mesenchymal stem cells), and how do these relate to FTO restoration specifically?
Do these sources report effects of FTO restoration (overexpression or epigenetic editing) on DNA damage markers, and if so, which markers and what direction of change?

Which of these interventions to restore FTO are via direct overexpression (transgene/plasmid) versus via epigenetic editing (e.g., CRISPRa) versus via indirect approaches (e.g., stem cell exosomes, small molecules)? According to these sources, which approach shows the strongest phenotype reversal?

What gaps remain in these sources regarding FTO restoration specifically via epigenetic/CRISPRa-based methods (as opposed to plasmid overexpression), and regarding senescence/DNA-damage phenotype reversal specifically in granulosa cells?
